title.narrative: The 12th Session of the World Urban Forum in Cairo, Egypt

description.narrative:
Project Description With over half of the global population living in cities, the rapid urbanization and its impact on communities, economies, climate change and policies are among the most pressing - concerns facing the world today. Acknowledging this, the New Urban Agenda, adopted during the United Nations Conference on Housing and Sustainable Urban Development (Habitat III) held in Quito, Ecuador, in October 2016, and following the agreement on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, including the Sustainable Development Goals, the positive correlation between well planned and managed cities and sustainable development is now recognized. For the successful realization of the New Urban Agenda’s vision for inclusive, prosperous, and environmentally sustainable cities, a collaborative effort involving diverse stakeholders and the general public is imperative. This implementation must be closely monitored based on a strong follow-up and review process of the New Urban Agenda. The existing knowledge and capacity, if adequately steered, nurtured, and exchanged together with the political commitment expressed by Member States in Quito at Habitat III are promising pre-requisites. In this context, the World Urban Forum established by the United Nations pursuant to paragraph 10 of resolution 18/5 of February 2001, is progressively consolidating its global relevance. The World Urban Forum was set up to examine one of the most pressing issues facing the world: rapid urbanization and its impact on communities, cities, economies, and climate change. Over the past two decades, WUF has evolved into the premier global conference on sustainable urbanization. Convened by the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat), the forum is a unique non-legislative platform and one of the most inclusive international gatherings on urban issues. The first WUF was held in Nairobi, Kenya in 2002 and has been held around the world ever since. Project Approach The proposed project strategy aims to consolidate the World Urban Forum as a permanent advocacy, partnership and knowledge platform contributing to the implementation, monitoring and review of the New Urban Agenda and the urban dimensions of the Sustainable Development Goals, as well as to the strategy and work of UN-Habitat. The first element of the strategy will be to strengthen the sustainability of the project, maintaining a high brand value, and securing sufficient funds by the contributions of host cities/countries. Predictability of funds will ensure staff continuity in the World Urban Forum Secretariat, including its decentralized presence in the regional offices. Bidding processes and funds should be secured a minimum of two years prior to any scheduled edition of the Forum. The WUF programme cycle allows the alignment of each edition with the current strategic plan and institutional priorities, while maintaining flexibility in the theme and structure to be tailored to suit future institutional priorities and the Strategic Plan. High-level participation, engagement, and promotion coupled with innovative formats and effective mechanisms to capture inputs will be put in place to enhance the implementation and follow up of the New Urban Agenda and the strategy and work of UN-Habitat. The results-based management approach of the programme will continue to be strengthened by developing specific indicators to measure the progress in advancing UN-Habitat work and strategy, as well as impacts in the implementation of the New Urban Agenda and the urban dimensions of the Sustainable Development Goals. Key components of the programme include partnerships, networking, resource mobilization and innovative capacity building. Strengthened online interactive platforms will also be key mechanisms for mobilization, engagement and data/information gathering, contributing to the progress report on the implementation of the New Urban Agenda. With this in consideration, a set of targeted strategies has been developed to ensure the achievement of the World Urban Forum’s objectives
Mobilization strategy: Embarking on the new cycle, the World Urban Forum introduces a dynamic mobilization strategy, with the objective of encouraging member states to integrate urban policies into national development plans. This includes multi-level urban forums and regional advocacy activities, strengthening the commitment of member states. This commitment and renewed engagement with UN-Habitat, will be consolidated through missions or UNH regional offices. Such actions will be integral to yearly reporting on SDG11 and the New Urban Agenda.
Communication strategies: The World Urban Forum’s communication strategy is a dynamic plan crafted to elevate the WUF’s impact and its global reach. Rooted in the WUF’s commitment to sustainable urban development, this strategy represents a proactive framework designed to; assert the premier status of WUF; expand the audience reach targeting groups
